convertibility_reason: EA relies on real-time WebRequest to Google Finance for external price data, uses timer-driven (not bar-driven) logic at 10-second intervals, reconstructs price history from scraped web quotes in a custom array (not MT5 bars), and implements time-delayed position closure based on externally-derived DeelayPosition. The trading signal depends entirely on an external web scraping mechanism that cannot be replicated in a standard backtesting/Python environment without a live Google Finance data feed.

other_exits: Time-based exit: position is closed via trade.PositionClose(_Symbol) when (TimeCurrent() - StartTime) >= DeelayPosition, where DeelayPosition is the time gap between the historical reference price and the current price in the Google Finance quote array
Session-based reset: when Google Finance session is closed, all positions are closed, CountPos is reset to 0, and the EA reinitializes via OnInit()

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Count input limits total positions opened per session (default 5). CountPos increments on each successful trade. When CountPos==Count, no new trades are opened.

custom_logic_notes: This EA scrapes Google Finance web pages via WebRequest every 10 seconds (timer interval) to obtain an external quote price. It maintains a FIFO array (ArrayQuote) of [price, timestamp] pairs. Trading logic: it finds a reference price (HistoryPrice) from GoogleFinanceHistoryMins minutes ago, then compares the latest scraped price (DiffPrice) against HistoryPrice +/- BarSize. If DiffPrice > HistoryPrice + BarSize, it buys; if DiffPrice < HistoryPrice - BarSize, it sells. After entering, it closes the position after DeelayPosition seconds (the time gap between the historical and current quote timestamps). Day-of-week filtering is implemented via Monday-Friday boolean inputs. The EA reinitializes itself (calling OnInit()) when the Google Finance session closes or on disabled trading days. The SL is extremely wide (5000 ticks) vs the TP (10 ticks), making this a high-R:R ratio strategy where the primary exit mechanism is the time-based close rather than TP/SL. sessionOpened bug: line 121 assigns sessionOpened=sessionOpened (self-assignment), so it never properly initializes from the constructor call.
python_conversion_notes: This EA is fundamentally incompatible with standard backtesting frameworks because: (1) It depends on real-time web scraping of Google Finance which no longer provides the same API format, (2) The signal source is an external price feed (not MT5 indicators or bar data), (3) Entry/exit timing is based on the delay between external quote timestamps, not bar boundaries, (4) The DeelayPosition exit is a time-based close derived from the gap between two externally-sourced timestamps. To convert to Python, you would need to: replace Google Finance scraping with an alternative real-time data source API, implement the FIFO price array logic, replicate the 10-second polling mechanism, and reconstruct the FindHistoryPrice/FIFO array traversal logic. The SL of 5000 ticks vs TP of 10 ticks means the actual profit mechanism is the time-based exit (DeelayPosition), not the TP hit.
